newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Friday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's 1330 GMT release of the U.S. November durable goods figures for November, which is forecast to show an increase of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.3 percent gain reported in October.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the (U.S. November) durable goods figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Thursday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2, six-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
